database_summary: This is a normalized OLTP-style product/order database (Northwind-like) implemented in SQLite. It contains customer, employee, supplier, product and order entities plus supporting lookup tables (categories, region, shippers, territories, usstates) and many-to-many bridge tables (customercustomerdemo, employeeterritories). The schema records orders and order_details as transactional/evental facts, products and suppliers as descriptive catalogs, and small reference tables for segmentation and thresholds. Row counts indicate moderate historic order volume (orders: 830, order_details: 2155).

accepted.name: order_line_revenue
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  orderid,
  productid,
  unitprice,
  quantity,
  discount,
  (unitprice * quantity) AS line_gross,
  (unitprice * quantity * (1.0 - discount)) AS line_net
FROM order_details
accepted.description: One row per order line (orderid, productid) with computed monetary measures. Use when aggregating sales, computing revenue, discounts, or joining to orders/products for higher-level rollups. | Use for: Total revenue per order / per customer / per product; Average discount or discount impact on revenue; Top-selling products by revenue or quantity; Order-level profitability and line-item breakdowns

accepted.name: orders_with_customer_employee_shipper
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.orderid,
  o.customerid,
  o.employeeid,
  o.orderdate,
  o.requireddate,
  o.shippeddate,
  o.shipvia,
  o.freight,
  o.shipname,
  o.shipaddress,
  o.shipcity,
  o.shipregion,
  o.shippostalcode,
  o.shipcountry,
  c.companyname AS companyname,
  c.contactname AS contactname,
  c.city AS city,
  c.region AS region,
  c.country AS country,
  e.lastname AS lastname,
  e.firstname AS firstname,
  e.title AS title,
  s.companyname AS shipper_companyname,
  s.phone AS phone
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customerid = c.customerid
LEFT JOIN employees e ON o.employeeid = e.employeeid
LEFT JOIN shippers s ON o.shipvia = s.shipperid
accepted.description: Denormalized one-row-per-order combining orders with customer, employee (sales rep) and shipper info where available. Use when analyzing orders alongside customer geography, employee responsible, or shipper attributes. | Use for: Order counts or revenue by customer geography; Employee sales performance (orders handled); Shipping performance or carrier analysis; Customer order histories with contextual contact info

accepted.name: product_catalog
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.productid,
  p.productname,
  p.supplierid,
  p.categoryid,
  p.quantityperunit,
  p.unitprice,
  p.unitsinstock,
  p.unitsonorder,
  p.reorderlevel,
  p.discontinued,
  c.categoryname AS categoryname,
  s.companyname AS supplier_companyname,
  s.country AS supplier_country
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN categories c ON p.categoryid = c.categoryid
LEFT JOIN suppliers s ON p.supplierid = s.supplierid
accepted.description: One row per product exposing product attributes along with category and supplier descriptive columns. Canonicalizes the product row for reporting or joins to sales facts. | Use for: Inventory reports (stock levels, reorder needs); Price lists and supplier-country analysis; Category-level product lists and joins to sales

accepted.name: customer_order_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customerid,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderid) AS orders_count,
  SUM(ol.line_net) AS total_revenue,
  SUM(ol.line_gross) AS total_gross,
  AVG(ol.line_net) AS avg_order_line_net
FROM orders o
JOIN order_line_revenue ol ON o.orderid = ol.orderid
GROUP BY o.customerid
accepted.description: One row per customer with aggregated order and revenue measures computed from order lines. Use for customer lifetime value, segmentation, or threshold bucketing. | Use for: Customer lifetime value or revenue segmentation; Identify high-value customers for targeting; Compare customer order frequency and average spend

accepted.name: product_sales_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.productid,
  p.productname,
  SUM(ol.line_net) AS product_revenue,
  SUM(ol.quantity) AS product_quantity,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(ol.line_net) DESC) AS rank_by_revenue,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(ol.quantity) DESC) AS rank_by_quantity
FROM products p
JOIN order_line_revenue ol ON p.productid = ol.productid
GROUP BY p.productid, p.productname
accepted.description: One row per product per periodless overall sales rank based on revenue and quantity. Exposes rank_by_revenue and rank_by_quantity to enable downstream Top-K filtering without embedding a LIMIT. | Use for: Top-selling products by revenue or quantity; Catalog pruning or promotion candidate selection; Trend analysis when adapted to time-windowed ranks

accepted.name: employee_sales_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.employeeid,
  e.lastname,
  e.firstname,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderid) AS orders_handled,
  SUM(ol.line_net) AS total_revenue,
  AVG(ol.line_net) AS avg_line_revenue
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employeeid = o.employeeid
LEFT JOIN order_line_revenue ol ON o.orderid = ol.orderid
GROUP BY e.employeeid, e.lastname, e.firstname
accepted.description: One row per employee summarizing orders handled and sales revenue. Useful for performance dashboards and commission calculations. Preserves employee identifiers for joins to HR info. | Use for: Sales rep performance and ranking; Workload analysis (orders per employee); Linking employee metrics to territories or regions

accepted.name: territory_employee_map
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  et.employeeid,
  et.territoryid,
  t.territorydescription AS territorydescription,
  t.regionid AS regionid
FROM employeeterritories et
LEFT JOIN territories t ON et.territoryid = t.territoryid
accepted.description: One row per employee-territory assignment exposing territory description and region. Use when analyzing sales or assignments by territory/region. | Use for: Mapping sales by territory/region; Allocating employee responsibilities or headcount by area; Joining employee performance to territory attributes

accepted.name: orders_running_revenue
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.orderid,
  o.orderdate,
  SUM(ol.line_net) AS order_revenue,
  SUM(SUM(ol.line_net)) OVER (ORDER BY o.orderdate, o.orderid ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN order_line_revenue ol ON o.orderid = ol.orderid
GROUP BY o.orderid, o.orderdate
accepted.description: One row per order with a running total of revenue ordered by orderdate. Useful for cumulative sales dashboards and trend displays. Exposes running_revenue so consumers can filter to any prefix. | Use for: Cumulative sales over time; Period-to-date comparisons and thresholds; Visualizing revenue growth as an accumulating series
